title: Pilot plan: customer VPC snapshot retention experiment
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc describes a 3-week pilot to validate a minimal snapshot retention model for customer-managed VPCs and a lightweight approval lane that surfaces high-risk changes for human review. Goal is to find pragmatic defaults for: (1) how much evidence (network snapshots, ACL diffs, operator notes) we retain locally at the control plane, (2) an approval-lane UX that avoids noisy interrupts for low-risk changes, and (3) a summarization pipeline to keep stored audit payloads compact and queryable for forensics.

Background / motivation:
- Customers onboarding to Private often push large amounts of networking metadata (BGP, route tables, firewall rules, NAT translations) during initial handoff. Storing full raw snapshots for every change is expensive and rarely required.
- Security teams want reproducible evidence for post-incident analysis: a small set of timed artifacts is often sufficient if we capture the right deltas, hashes, and operator annotations.
- We need an operational approval gate for changes that escalate risk (e.g., opening public ingress, changing outbound egress CIDR, adding new peering). Current designs either: (a) block too aggressively and slow onboarding, or (b) accept everything and leave no durable audit trail.

Pilot scope (what we'll test):
- Environments: 3 customers (1 enterprise, 2 mid-market) in Dedicated/private mode who consent to pilot capture.
- Ingested sources: customer-provided VPC config snapshots (JSON), NAT/peering change events, operator CLI annotations, and route table diffs from the edge agent.
- Retention experiment variants:
  * Variant A (short): keep 7-day raw snapshots, generate compact delta records stored 90 days.
  * Variant B (medium): keep 30-day raw snapshots, compact deltas 365 days.
  * Variant C (compact-only): no raw snapshots retained beyond 24 hours; keep enriched deltas 365 days + cryptographic digest of raw for validation.
- Approval lane behavior:
  * Passive lane: low-risk changes auto-commit and generate summarized evidence.
  * Active lane: high-risk changes require explicit approval by an operator in console (can be a delegated approver).
  * Escalation rules are policy-driven (see Policy examples below).

Success metrics (how we measure):
- Operational cost delta: measured change in storage/ingest cost for pilot customers vs. baseline (per-customer monthly). Target: >= 45% storage reduction for Variant C vs baseline.
- Investigator efficacy: time-to-evidence for a simulated incident (search & fetch). Target: <= 10 minutes for first evidence bundle retrieval in >= 90% of simulated incidents.
- False positive/negative approvals: pilot approval lane should present <10% unnecessary manual approvals (low-risk misclassifications) and <5% missed escalations in policy-simulated tests.
- Customer satisfaction: Net promoter question in pilot wrap: "Did evidence retrieval meet your expectations?" target 4/5 average.

Data model and summarization approach:
- Raw snapshot: full JSON config (if retained); stored S3 path + SHA256 digest.
- Delta record (compact): list of changed keys + small context (string snippets up to 512 bytes), timestamp, actor, and a reference digest of the raw snapshot. Compact payload limited to ~8KB compressed per change.
- Enriched evidence bundle: compact delta(s) + operator note(s) + system-calculated risk score + policy decision (auto/approved/rejected) + signed checkpoint (control plane key).
- Indexing keys: customer_id, tenant_id, change_time, change_type, risk_tags, digest.

Policy examples (pilot rules):
- High risk (requires approval): any inbound rule that permits 0.0.0.0/0 to port ranges {22, 2376, 9090} OR adding a peering to a CIDR outside approved list.
- Medium risk (passive with telemetry): removing an SG rule that previously blocked outbound to a monitored subnet.
- Low risk: routine metadata changes (tag updates, description text) are auto-committed.

Approval UX / operator flow (sketch):
- Console shows compact diff card with: snippets of removed/added rules, risk score, suggested mitigation, and a 1-click Approve / Reject.
- For approval requests, send an ephemeral approval token to the approver; token valid 30 minutes. Expiring token triggers auto-revert option if policy chosen.
- Audit note required for approvals that reduce existing guardrails (free text, minimal 140 chars).

Forensics and retrieval playbook:
- Incident investigator flow: search by timeframe -> fetch compact evidence bundles -> if raw snapshot digest exists and is needed, request raw rehydration (policy-limited; rehydration logs an event and increments retention billing).
- Retention audit trail: every rehydration prints a signed checkpoint with actor, reason, and timestamp. We keep rehydration logs for the lifetime of the compact delta.

Operational constraints and cost controls:
- Hard throttle: raw snapshot rehydration limited to 5 rehydrates per customer per 24 hours during pilot (to contain cost).
- Billing model: pilot customers are offered reduced rehydration fees; production pricing TBD.
- Storage tiering: older raw snapshots move to cold storage (cheaper, slower) after 7 days for Variant B/C.

Telemetry and observability needs:
- Per-change metrics: change_type, risk_score, auto/approved, commit_latency, storage_bytes_raw, storage_bytes_compact.
- Dashboards: approval queue length, mean approval wait time, rehydration counts.
- Alerting: escalation if approval queue > 50 items for > 15 minutes or mean wait time > 20m for high-risk items.

Security and compliance notes:
- Sensitive fields (e.g., credentials captured accidentally in snapshots) must be redacted via a scrubber before compacting. The scrubber rules are configurable and applied prior to storage.
- All evidence bundles signed by control-plane KMS key. Customers get signed digest receipts for legal purposes.

Open questions / Risks:
- Do customers accept digest-only preservation for legal/regulatory audits in some jurisdictions? Need legal review per pilot customer.
- How to handle agent discrepancies (edge agent vs. control plane snapshot mismatch)? Propose: attach confidence score and agent-provided sequence numbers.
- Performance risk: rehydration spikes could overload the API; mitigation: queue and backoff + rate-limited worker pool.

Pilot timeline (3 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep, 1 week): finalize policy set, instrument scrubber, implement compact delta encoder, test storage lifecycle.
- Week 1: onboard Customer A (enterprise) to Variant B; run baseline capture and verify indexing/search.
- Week 2: onboard Customers B & C to Variant A and C; run simulated incidents and approval stress tests; gather telemetry.
- Week 3: analyze metrics, conduct investigator time trials, collect customer feedback, prepare recommendations.

Key milestones and owners:
- Policy definition doc (owner: Linh Tran) due 2025-01-21.
- Scrubber v1 (owner: Diego Alvarez) deploy to staging 2025-01-24.
- Compact encoder (owner: Evan Morales) feature branch + integration tests 2025-01-20.
- Console approval UX prototype (owner: Priya Shah) staged 2025-01-28.

Next steps (immediate):
- Quick sync with security/legal to confirm digest-acceptability per-customer (action: Priya).
- Create JIRA epic PD-4821 with sub-tasks for implementation and test matrix (action: Linh).
- Schedule pilot onboarding call with Customer A (action: Sara).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This is intentionally lightweight — aim is to reduce storage and still have usable forensic evidence. I expect policy hysteresis will need tuning; please flag any must-have legal requirements early.
- If we see too many rehydration requests in early testing, we should add a pre-authorization step for rehydrates from security teams.

Appendix: small example compact delta (conceptual):
- change_time: 2025-01-11T17:12:34Z
- actor: cloud-runner/edge-agent-32
- changed_keys: ["vpc.firewallRules[12]", "vpc.peering[3].allowedCidrs"]
- snippet_added: "allow tcp 8080 from 10.4.0.0/16"
- snippet_removed: "deny tcp 22 from 0.0.0.0/0"
- risk_score: 78
- decision: AUTO_COMMIT
- raw_digest: sha256:ab12...

Please review policies inline and add any regulatory constraints for pilot customers.
